h: Before You Step on the Ice
p: Ice skating is one of those activities where a few minutes of preparation pay off big time. Start with the boots: they should be snug, with laces tight around the ankle so your foot doesn't roll inside. If they hurt or feel loose, swap them before you head out. Wear thin socks that come up past the top of the boot, and leave the trainer socks at home.

On the ice, keep your knees soft and your arms out a bit for balance. Short, gentle pushes are better than big strides when you're starting out. Falling is part of the fun, but if you do go down, tuck your fingers in and get up quickly so nobody skates over them. It's worth telling the kids this one before you start.
If your group catches the bug, the Blaze home games are a great reason to come back. Watching the pros fly round the same ice you've just been wobbling on gives you a whole new respect for them.

Coventry's compact city centre makes it easy to fill the rest of your day. The Coventry Transport Museum is a must for car and bike fans, with a huge collection celebrating the city's motoring history, and it's free to get in. The Herbert Art Gallery and Museum sits close to the cathedral, with exhibitions on local history and art. Wander the old streets around Spon Street for a glimpse of medieval Coventry, and you'll find plenty of spots for a bite between skates and sightseeing.
